records.jp: 星崎さん、人はどうしてお参りをするんでしょう？<CR>知識としては、知っているのですが……
records.en_original: Ao, why do you think people pray? I know the basic reason, of course, but I'd like to hear what you think.
records.en: Hoshizaki-san, why do people visit shrines to pray?<CR>I know the explanation as knowledge, but...

records.jp: んー。神様にお祈りして、<CR>お願いを叶えてもらうため……かなぁ
records.en_original: Hmm. I guess to get their wishes granted by the gods?
records.en: Hmm.<CR>I guess to get their wishes granted by the gods?

records.jp: 神様……つまり、思い入れやすい神を選んで、<CR>そこに祈るという形で自己暗示をかける……
records.en_original: The gods... Seems to me that prayer is just a form of autosuggestion. Believers are convinced they'll get the things they ask for...
records.en: The gods... In other words, people choose a god they can invest<CR>their feelings in and pray there to induce autosuggestion...

records.jp: そういうことなのだとは思いますが、<CR>何故そう上手く自己暗示がかけられるのか、疑問です
records.en_original: At least that's what I think. Still, autosuggestion does seem to be surprisingly effective.
records.en: I think that is what happens,<CR>but I wonder why people are able to induce autosuggestion so effectively.

records.jp: へ？　自己暗示？
records.en_original: Huh? Autosuggestion?
records.en: Huh? Autosuggestion?

records.jp: ……違うんでしょうか？
records.en_original: Am I wrong?
records.en: Am I wrong?

records.jp: 言われてみれば、そうとも言える気がするけど、<CR>うーん……
records.en_original: I guess you could think of it like that, but... Hmm...
records.en: I guess you could think of it like that, but...<CR>Hmm...

records.jp: ……では、お祈りをすればそれが叶うと<CR>みなさんは本当に信じているんでしょうか？
records.en_original: Then do people truly believe that their prayers will be answered?
records.en: Then do people truly believe<CR>that their prayers will be answered?

records.jp: うーん。そうとは言い切れないけど……<CR>多分、祈ることが大切なんだよ
records.en_original: I don't think I'd go that far. I think it's the act itself that's important.
records.en: I don't think I'd go that far.<CR>I think it's the act itself that's important.

records.jp: 祈ることが……ですか？<CR>自己暗示とは、どう違うのでしょう？
records.en_original: The act of prayer? How is it different from simple autosuggestion?
records.en: The act of prayer?<CR>How is it different from simple autosuggestion?

records.jp: そうだなぁ……違わないのかも。<CR>私が自己暗示って発想、いままで無かっただけで
records.en_original: Well... Maybe it's not. I've just never thought about it that way.
records.en: Well... Maybe it's not.<CR>I've just never thought about it that way.

records.jp: だから、なんかすごい新鮮だった！
records.en_original: I think your perspective is pretty interesting!
records.en: I think your perspective is pretty interesting!

records.jp: 私の発想……変だとは、思わないんですか？<CR>
records.en_original: You don't think that my way of thinking is...strange?
records.en: You do not think my way of thinking is strange?<CR>

records.jp: え、なんで変？<CR>詩さんって頭いい……ってなったけど
records.en_original: Huh? Why would I? I was just thinking that you sure are smart.
records.en: Huh? Why is that strange?<CR>I just thought, 'You're smart, Uta-san...'

records.jp: うん。自己暗示で元気出すって、アリかもだよね！<CR>お参りって、もともとそのためのものだし
records.en_original: I don't think it's so bad to call it that! I think that's pretty much the reason for it.
records.en: Yes. Cheering yourself up through autosuggestion might be valid!<CR>Shrine visits were originally for that sort of thing, after all.

records.jp: 私……もともとはお祈りってさ、<CR>願う気持ちの背中を押してくれるって思っててさ
records.en_original: I think that sometimes it gives us the courage to do things we normally wouldn't.
records.en: Originally,<CR>I thought prayer gave a push to the feelings behind a person's wish.

records.jp: 背中を……押してくれる、ですか？
records.en_original: Courage?
records.en: Courage?

records.jp: うん。神様を信じるかはともかくだけど、<CR>なんか、元気が出る気がしてさ
records.en_original: Yeah. It doesn't matter whether I actually believe or not, it gave me that little push I needed.
records.en: Yes. Whether or not I believe in a god,<CR>praying somehow makes me feel more energetic.

records.jp: ……私は星崎さんに、背中を押してもらっています。<CR>それは、自己暗示とは違う気がします
records.en_original: You've done the same for me, Ao. You give me courage. I don't believe that is autosuggestion.
records.en: You are the one who gives me a push, Hoshizaki-san.<CR>That feels different from autosuggestion.

records.jp: ですから……
records.en_original: So...
records.en: So...

records.jp: お参りには、意味があるのかもしれませんね
records.en_original: Perhaps, there is some meaning to prayer after all.
records.en: Perhaps, there is some meaning to prayer after all.

records.jp: きっと、信じてるんじゃないかなぁ。<CR>むしろ、信じたいっていうか？
records.en_original: I think they do. Or maybe, it's that they want to.
records.en: I think they do.<CR>Or maybe, it's that they want to.

records.jp: 私も「次の試験で赤点取りませんようにー」とか、<CR>マジで祈っちゃうし、それでどうにかなる気になるし
records.en_original: I usually pray for stuff like passing my next exam. When I pray really, really hard, it makes me feel like everything will work out.
records.en: I usually pray for stuff like passing my next exam.<CR>When I pray really, really hard, it makes me feel like everything will work out.

records.jp: それって、自己暗示ってヤツだよね！<CR>でも、それで頑張れる自分、すごいかも……
records.en_original: I think that's basically what autosuggestion is, right? I think it's actually pretty cool being able to motivate yourself like that.
records.en: I think that's basically what autosuggestion is, right?<CR>I think it's actually pretty cool being able to motivate yourself like that.

records.jp: 祈りという行為が、行動する気持ちを強める……<CR>ということでしょうか？
records.en_original: You mean that the act of prayer gives them the courage to act?
records.en: You mean that the act of prayer gives them<CR>the courage to act?

records.jp: かもだね。<CR>うーん、侮れないな。自己暗示……！
records.en_original: I think you could see it that way. I guess autosuggestion is a pretty powerful thing!
records.en: I think you could see it that way.<CR>I guess autosuggestion is a pretty powerful thing!

records.jp: ふふ。<CR>星崎さんには、少し似合わない気がします
records.en_original: Hehe... That seems a bit unlike you, Ao.
records.en: Hehe...<CR>That seems a bit unlike you, Hoshizaki-san.

records.jp: え、そうかな？
records.en_original: Really?
records.en: Really?

records.jp: 星崎さんは、そんなものが無くても<CR>自分の行動を決められる人だと思いますから……
records.en_original: You don't seem like the type who needs something like that to motivate yourself.
records.en: Because I think you're someone who can decide<CR>how to act even without something like that, Hoshizaki-san...

records.jp: えっとさ……<CR>詩さん、私のこと褒めすぎてない！？
records.en_original: Er... Don't you think you're giving me too much credit?
records.en: Um...<CR>Uta-san, aren't you praising me too much!?

records.jp: 私は……人を褒めるということが上手くできません。<CR>どれも嘘になってしまいそうです
records.en_original: I have found that my compliments often come off as sounding disingenuous.
records.en: I am... not good at praising people.<CR>It feels as though any compliment I give would become a lie.

records.jp: 褒めると……嘘になる？
records.en_original: What do you mean?
records.en: What do you mean?

records.jp: はい。褒め言葉は、相手を喜ばせる言葉です。<CR>本心ではなくても使うものではないでしょうか？
records.en_original: Compliments are words meant to delight another person. This is difficult if you cannot understand what will delight them.
records.en: Yes. A compliment is a phrase meant to please the other person.<CR>Is it not something people use even when it does not reflect their true feelings?

records.jp: もー！　詩さんって、正直者すぎるー！<CR>私、詩さんが騙されないようにお祈りしよう！
records.en_original: Geez! You're way too honest, Uta! I'll have to pray that I don't get sweet talked by you!
records.en: Honestly, Uta-san, you are far too honest!<CR>I will pray that no one deceives you!

records.jp: 正直……そんなに良い人間ではないと思いますが、<CR>では私は、私の言葉が嘘にならないように……
records.en_original: Honest...? I'm not sure if that really applies to me. Perhaps my prayer should be that my words sound genuine...
records.en: Honest... I do not think I am such a good person.<CR>Then I will pray that my words do not become lies...

records.jp: でも、私は本当に祈るということができるでしょうか。<CR>……少し、自信がありません
records.en_original: Though, I wonder if I'm even able to pray... I'm sure how to do this.
records.en: But am I truly capable of praying? I am...<CR>not very confident.

records.jp: うーん。形から入ってみるのもアリだと思うよ！<CR>意外と湧いてくるかもしれないしさ
records.en_original: Hmm... I don't think there's anything special you have to do. I think just trying is the most important thing!
records.en: Hmm. I think it is fine to begin by going through the motions!<CR>The feeling might arise unexpectedly.

records.jp: ……そういうもの、でしょうか？
records.en_original: You think...?
records.en: You think...?

records.jp: うん。物は試しだよ！
records.en_original: Yep! Fake it till you make it!
records.en: Yes. There is no harm in trying!

records.jp: ふふ。星崎さんらしい言い方ですね。<CR>でも、試してみる気持ちになりました
records.en_original: Hehe. What a very Ao thing to say. All right then, I'll give it a try.
records.en: Hehe. What a very Hoshizaki-san thing to say.<CR>All right then, I'll give it a try.

records.jp: 詩さんなら、できると思うよ。<CR>信じて願う気持ち、もう持ってるもん
records.en_original: I know you can do it. All you have to do is have faith and a desire. I know you at least have that.
records.en: I think you can do it, Uta-san.<CR>You already have the desire to believe and wish.

records.jp: 私が……ですか？<CR>
records.en_original: I do...?
records.en: Me...?<CR>

records.jp: うん。だってさ、私だったら詩さんのココロトープ、<CR>最初ので挫折する気がするもん
records.en_original: Yeah. If I were you, I don't know if I could have kept going after seeing what you saw when you first entered your Heartscape.
records.en: Yeah. If it were me, I think I'd have given up after the first part of your Heartscape,<CR>Uta-san.

records.jp: それでも詩さんは、自分の過去や記憶を知りたいって<CR>願ってくれたんだ
records.en_original: But even after all that, you still were determined to get all your memories back.
records.en: Even so, you wished to learn about your past and memories,<CR>Uta-san.

records.jp: あの気持ちが「願う」という気持ちだとしたら……
records.en_original: Was that desire that I felt then?
records.en: If that feeling was what it means to wish...

records.jp: …………<CR>そうですね。私にもできるかもしれません
records.en_original: ...Yes, I think I can do this.
records.en: ...Yes,<CR>I think I can do this.

records.jp: それじゃ、いい？
records.en_original: Ready?
records.en: Ready?

records.jp: はい
records.en_original: Yes.
records.en: Yes.

records.jp: それじゃ、あとは手を合わせて祈るだけ。<CR>あ、ホントはお祀りしてる神様に祈るんだけど……
records.en_original: Now all that's left is putting your hands together and praying. Oh, usually you have to thinking about the deity that's enshrined, but...
records.en: Then all that remains is to put your hands together and pray.<CR>Ah, normally you would pray to the deity enshrined here, but...

records.jp: いまは深く考えないで、ただ自分の願いを<CR>叶えたいって思うだけでいいと思うよ
records.en_original: Don't overthink it. Just focus on your wish.
records.en: Don't overthink it.<CR>Just focus on your wish.

records.jp: ふふ……不信仰の極み、と言われそうですね。<CR>でも、私にはちょうどいい気がします
records.en_original: Hehe... I don't think this is what most people consider prayer, but I think it may be perfect for me.
records.en: Hehe... Someone might call this the height of impiety.<CR>But I think it suits me.

records.jp: これでよしっと！
records.en_original: And we're done!
records.en: And we're done!

records.jp: どんな感じ？
records.en_original: So, how was it?
records.en: So, how was it?

records.jp: 願いを思い浮かべることができました
records.en_original: I discovered something to pray for.
records.en: I was able to picture a wish in my mind.

records.jp: そっか。よかった。<CR>実現したいなって気持ちになれた？
records.en_original: That's great Did you feel like it gave you the courage to try and make that a reality?
records.en: I see. I am glad.<CR>Did it make you feel that you wanted to make it come true?

records.jp: そうですね……不思議なことですが、確かにひとりで<CR>心の中で願っているより、強く願えた気がします
records.en_original: It's strange... I do feel like I was able to wish harder than if I was to simply think about it myself.
records.en: It's strange...<CR>I do feel like I was able to wish harder than if I was to simply think about it myself.

records.jp: なにより……星崎さんが、こんな機会を作って<CR>くれた事に、感謝しています
records.en_original: More than anything else, I'm thankful for this opportunity you've given me.
records.en: More than anything...<CR>I'm grateful that you created this opportunity, Hoshizaki-san.

records.jp: そ、そんなたいしたことしてないってば……
records.en_original: I-it's not that big a deal...
records.en: I-it's not that big a deal...

records.jp: ありがとう、付き合ってくれて
records.en_original: Thanks for coming with me.
records.en: Thanks for coming with me.

records.jp: いえ。私も星崎さんのおかげで、願うということを<CR>より大切に思うことができたと思います
records.en_original: You're welcome. Thank you for teaching more about these things.
records.en: No. Thanks to you, Hoshizaki-san,<CR>I think I've come to value wishing even more.

records.jp: 私にも、願うことができて……嬉しいです。<CR>星崎さんは、いつも私に勇気をくれますね
records.en_original: I'm...happy that I was able to do this. You always give me confidence, Ao.
records.en: I'm...happy that I was able to do this.<CR>You always give me confidence, Hoshizaki-san.

records.jp: そんな、大層なことしてるつもりなんか<CR>ないんだけど……
records.en_original: I don't think I've done anything special...
records.en: I don't think I've done anything<CR>special...

records.jp: でも、詩さんの笑顔が見れたから、満足かな！
records.en_original: But as long as I get to see your smile, that's enough for me!
records.en: But I got to see you smile, Uta-san, so I'm satisfied!

records.jp: 私の笑顔を見ると満足……ですか？<CR>よく、分かりません
records.en_original: It is...? I'm sorry, I'm not sure I understand.
records.en: You are satisfied when you see me smile...?<CR>I do not really understand.

records.jp: フラグメント「<CLGR>%s<CLNR>」を<CR>手に入れました
records.en_original: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR> Fragment.
records.en: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR><CR>Fragment.
